speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the information; since this is a newborn with a generalized rash, can you describe the appearance of the rash and whether it is present at birth or has developed since? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, CRP, Blood_Culture.

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Congenital Syphilis. The combination of a generalized maculopapular rash with pustules on an erythematous base, involving the trunk and extremities but sparing the palms and soles, is highly characteristic of secondary syphilis in a newborn. I have requested the Complete Blood Count, CRP, and Blood Culture to confirm the infection.
